metadata.subject: Operating Systems
metadata.title: Detect Deadlocks
metadata.description: Reason about resource requests, blocking, and true circular wait.

learning_objectives: Distinguish allocation edges from request edges.
Recognize recoverable blocking and true deadlock.
Explain why a cycle is decisive in the explicit one-instance model.

mission.title: Reason about resource requests
mission.description: Predict each request's real consequence in a one-instance resource model.

introduction.title: Holding and waiting can stop progress
introduction.content: A process may hold one resource while requesting another. If every process in a closed chain waits for the next, none can continue.
points: Resource → Process means the resource is allocated.
Process → Resource means the process is requesting it.
This lesson explicitly models one instance of every resource.

worked_example.title: A circular wait forms one request at a time
worked_example.content: A blocked process is not automatically deadlocked.

steps.explanation: P1 blocks because P2 holds R2, but P2 can still finish.
This request closes a circular wait.
With one instance of R1 and R2, neither process in the cycle can progress.

worked_example.conclusion: A cycle means deadlock here because every resource has exactly one instance; that rule is not universal for multi-instance systems.

next.title: Now predict it.
next.content: Inspect the allocation before deciding what each request causes.

action_explanations.predict-granted: A free resource can be granted immediately.
action_explanations.predict-blocked: A held resource blocks the requester, but blocking alone is not deadlock.
action_explanations.predict-deadlocked: The request closes a one-instance circular wait, so every process in the cycle is stuck.
action_explanations.predict-released: Releasing the resource allows a waiting request to progress.

actions.label: Inspect a held resource
actions.task: Does P1 block when it requests R2?

actions.label: Detect the closing request
actions.task: What happens when P2 also requests R1?

challenge.title: Blocking without deadlock
challenge.start_message: Decide whether each request is granted, blocked, or deadlocked.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Continue inspecting the graph.

phases.title: Separate blocking from deadlock
phases.instruction: Apply the one-instance allocation rules to both requests.
phases.feedback: Trace every request edge to the current holder.

items.content: A blocked request becomes deadlock only if it closes a wait cycle.

phases.title: Practice resource requests
phases.feedback: Blocking alone is not a cycle.

guidance.start_message: Trace a longer allocation chain with no hint.

phases.instruction: Track three processes and their directed relationships.

guidance.start_message: Determine exactly which request changes the classification.

phases.instruction: Classify each request without being shown the final graph.
phases.feedback: A one-way chain is recoverable; a closed cycle is not.

phases.instruction: Derive every consequence from the directed graph.

solve.title: Expert Deadlocks
solve.instruction: Diagnose the generated resource sequence with no hints.

quiz.question: P1 holds R1 and waits for R2. P2 holds R2 but requests nothing. What is this?

discovery.title: Deadlock discovery
discovery.summary: In this one-instance model, deadlock requires a closed circular wait; ordinary blocking can still be resolved.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: Deadlock means processes in a closed wait cycle cannot make progress.

sections.title: Edge directions
sections.content: Resource → Process is allocation. Process → Resource is a request.

sections.title: Why the assumption matters
sections.content: A cycle is decisive in this lesson because each resource has one instance. Multi-instance systems need a broader safety analysis.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Blocked does not automatically mean deadlocked; trace whether the wait chain closes.

alternate_explanations.title: Two locked toolboxes
alternate_explanations.content: Each worker holds one key and waits for the key held by the other. Neither can finish and release what they hold.

alternate_explanations.title: Trace the arrows
alternate_explanations.content: R1 → P1 → R2 → P2 → R1 closes a one-instance cycle, so P1 and P2 are deadlocked.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why is a blocked process not always deadlocked?
recall.model_answer: Blocking can end when the holder releases the resource. Deadlock needs a closed wait cycle where no participant can release what the next process needs.
